get.description:
Returns a cursor-paged feed of the caller's tenant appointments, newest changes first.
Pass `updatedSince` (UTC) to scope by change time and `pageSize` to size the page; follow
the `next` link (an opaque `cursor`) to page. Delivery is at-least-once — dedupe on `id`.

get.description:
Returns every payment mode configured for the authenticated tenant, ordered by `id` ascending, one page at a time.

This is a FULL-COLLECTION read, not an incremental feed. The underlying table has no created or modified timestamp, so there is deliberately no `updatedSince` parameter and no way to ask for "what changed": a consumer keeping a local copy re-reads the whole collection.

Deleted payment modes ARE included, carrying `isDeleted: true`. Historical payments keep referencing a mode after the practice removes it, so filtering them out server-side would leave those payments unresolvable. Filter on `isDeleted` for the currently selectable modes.

`name` and `displayName` are practice-authored labels and `id` is tenant-local; `paymentType` is the only field that means the same thing across tenants.

Returns every payment reason configured for the authenticated tenant, ordered by `id` ascending, one page at a time.

This is a FULL-COLLECTION read, not an incremental feed. The underlying table has no created or modified timestamp, so there is deliberately no `updatedSince` parameter and no way to ask for "what changed": a consumer keeping a local copy re-reads the whole collection.

Deleted AND inactive payment reasons ARE included, carrying `isDeleted` and `isActive`. Historical payments keep referencing a reason after the practice removes or deactivates it, so filtering either out server-side would leave those payments unresolvable. Filter on `isDeleted` and `isActive` for the currently selectable reasons.

`description` matches the inline reference object already carried on `/v1/financials/payments`.

Returns every discount reason configured for the authenticated tenant, ordered by `id` ascending, one page at a time.

This is a FULL-COLLECTION read, not an incremental feed. The underlying table has no created or modified timestamp, so there is deliberately no `updatedSince` parameter and no way to ask for "what changed": a consumer keeping a local copy re-reads the whole collection.

This table carries no delete flag at all, and deleting a discount reason is a HARD delete: a historical invoice, credit-note or estimate line can reference an id this endpoint no longer returns. The inline `{id, name}` object already published on those line items remains the only way to read a deleted reason's label.

`name` matches the inline reference object already carried on those line items.

Returns every occasion configured for the authenticated tenant, ordered by `id` ascending, one page at a time.

This is a FULL-COLLECTION read, not an incremental feed. The underlying table has no created or modified timestamp, so there is deliberately no `updatedSince` parameter and no way to ask for "what changed": a consumer keeping a local copy re-reads the whole collection.

There is no closed enum for the occasion: the set is tenant-extensible, so use `isSystem` to distinguish a platform-seeded occasion from one the practice created.

Deleted AND inactive occasions ARE included, carrying `isDeleted` and `isActive`. Historical records keep referencing an occasion after the practice removes or deactivates it, so filtering either out server-side would leave those records unresolvable. Filter on `isDeleted` and `isActive` for the currently selectable occasions.

Returns every brand configured for the authenticated tenant, ordered by `id` ascending, one page at a time.

This is a FULL-COLLECTION read, not an incremental feed. The underlying table has no created or modified timestamp, so there is deliberately no `updatedSince` parameter and no way to ask for "what changed": a consumer keeping a local copy re-reads the whole collection.

Deleted brands ARE included, carrying `isDeleted: true`. Historical items keep referencing a brand after the practice removes it, so filtering it out server-side would leave those items unresolvable. Filter on `isDeleted` for the currently selectable brands.

This is additive to the inline `brand` object already published on an item (`{ id, name }`), which is unchanged and stays.

Returns every category configured for the authenticated tenant, ordered by `id` ascending, one page at a time.

This is a FULL-COLLECTION read, not an incremental feed. The underlying table has no created or modified timestamp, so there is deliberately no `updatedSince` parameter and no way to ask for "what changed": a consumer keeping a local copy re-reads the whole collection.

This is the FLAT category list — the `Categories` table — and is NOT the hierarchical one. `HierarchicalCategories` is a separate table with its own `parentId` and its own delete flag, served by a separate lookup; do not confuse the two.

This table carries no delete flag at all, and deleting a category is a HARD delete: a historical item can carry a category id this endpoint no longer returns. The inline `categories[] { id, name }` array already published on that item remains the only way to read a deleted category's label.

`name` matches the inline reference objects already carried in that array.

Returns every hierarchical category configured for the authenticated tenant, ordered by `id` ascending, one page at a time.

This is a FULL-COLLECTION read, not an incremental feed. The underlying table has no created or modified timestamp, so there is deliberately no `updatedSince` parameter and no way to ask for "what changed": a consumer keeping a local copy re-reads the whole collection.

The collection is FLAT. `parentId` is nullable — null for a root category — and there is NO server-side tree assembly: a nested response cannot be cursor-paged coherently, because a page boundary would have to fall between a parent and a child it has already promised the consumer. Build the tree client-side from `id` and `parentId`.

Ordering is by `id`, NOT by tree position: a child can arrive on an EARLIER page than its parent. A consumer must read every page before assembling the tree, or it will observe a `parentId` that "does not exist yet" on a page it has already seen.

`parentId` MAY point at a category whose own `isDeleted` is `true`. The write side validates only that a parent id exists at all when a category is created or reparented, never that the parent is still live, so a live child can end up under a deleted parent. `parentId` may also point at a row a consumer's own picker logic has filtered out for some other reason. Resolve `parentId` against this same collection, including deleted rows, rather than assuming it always resolves to a currently-selectable category.

Deleted categories ARE included, carrying `isDeleted: true`, and are never filtered out server-side — for the reason above, a live child can depend on a deleted parent still being resolvable. Filter on `isDeleted` for the currently selectable categories.

This is additive to the inline `hierarchicalCategory` object already published on an item (`{ id, name, parentId }`), which is unchanged and stays. This is NOT the flat `Categories` lookup (`/v1/financials/item-categories`) — that is a separate table with no parent and no delete flag at all; do not confuse the two.

Returns every item type configured for the authenticated tenant, ordered by `id` ascending, one page at a time.

This is a FULL-COLLECTION read, not an incremental feed. The underlying table has no created or modified timestamp, so there is deliberately no `updatedSince` parameter and no way to ask for "what changed": a consumer keeping a local copy re-reads the whole collection.

The table also carries four behaviour flags — `showInventory`, `showPaymentSchedules`, `showCollection`, `isSelectable` — that drive internal UI behaviour, not the meaning of the type. NONE of them is published here.

Seeded defaults exist, but the set is tenant-extensible, so there is deliberately no closed enum for it.

This table carries no delete flag at all, and deleting an item type is a HARD delete: a historical item can carry an item-type id this endpoint no longer returns. The inline `itemType { id, name }` reference object already published on that item remains the only way to read a deleted item type's label.

The payload matches that inline `itemType` object exactly: `id` and `name`, nothing more.

Returns the tenant's estimates as a CHANGE FEED, one page at a time, ordered by `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)` ascending with the estimate id as a tie-break.

`modifiedDateUtc` carries that coalesced value and is therefore never null: the stored modified timestamp IS nullable and is null for every estimate nobody has edited, so an incremental consumer filtering on the raw column would never see them. Until the first edit, `modifiedDateUtc` equals `createdUtcDate`. The filter parameter is `updatedSince` while the response field is `modifiedDateUtc`; that asymmetry is deliberate and shared with the appointments public surface.

Filters: `updatedSince` (ISO-8601 timestamp, inclusive), `patientId`, `status` (repeatable — `status=Open&status=Funded` reads as OR), and `effectiveDateFrom` / `effectiveDateTo`, an inclusive range over the `effectiveDate` calendar date. `status` accepts exactly the values `/v1/financials/estimate-statuses` returns and rejects `Unknown`, which exists only to absorb a stored value from outside the contract on the way out.

Rejected, Cancelled, Deleted and expired estimates ARE included by default. Reporting computes conversion rates from the whole population, so excluding them server-side would remove the denominator; narrow with `status` instead. There is no revision history in the schema — an edit overwrites the estimate and moves its watermark — so every row here is the current version of that estimate.

One caveat when computing a conversion rate. A practice can CLONE an estimate, which creates a separate estimate with its own `estimateId` and `estimateNumber`, in `Draft`, and the schema records NO link back to the original — the only trace is an internal audit line, which this surface does not publish. A reworked quote therefore appears here as two independent estimates, and a naive rate over the whole population double-counts the opportunity. There is no server-side fix available: the relationship genuinely is not stored.

A cursor is bound to the filters it was issued under. Changing any filter value and replaying the cursor is rejected rather than silently resumed mid-stream in another patient's data.

Line items are INLINE, in `lineItems`, fetched set-based for the whole page. Note two things about them. `isCalculatedRate` says which arithmetic applies: when it is `false`, `subTotalAmount = rate × quantity − totalDiscount`; when it is `true`, `rate` IS the line total and that multiplication does not reconcile. `subTotalAmount` is authoritative either way. And `overrideName` is OPERATOR-AUTHORED FREE TEXT that MAY CONTAIN PHI — do not log it, cache it by it, or index it.

`invoiceIds` on the header is the distinct set of invoices this estimate's lines have been converted into; conversion is per line, so more than one id, or one id alongside a line whose `invoiceId` is null, means the estimate is PARTIALLY converted. Each id is retrievable from `/v1/financials/invoices/{id}`.

`serviceLocationId` and `billingLocationId` are `null` when the practice never set them. The underlying columns are `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and 0 is a not-set sentinel rather than a location id, so publishing it would name a location that does not exist.

Not published: patient signatures in any form, the tax breakdown, memberships, patient credits, responsible-party payer splits, and every operator free-text field other than `overrideName`.

`lineItems` IS BOUNDED. One page returns at most 25000 line rows in total across its estimates, and the single-estimate read is bounded the same way. The ceiling is orders of magnitude above any real estimate, so reaching it says something is wrong with the data rather than with the request. If it is ever reached the `lineItems` arrays on that page are truncated from the last estimate backwards — `next`, the paging keyset and the header fields are unaffected — and the service counts and logs the event rather than truncating in silence.

Returns one estimate with its line items inline — the same payload the collection returns, for a single id.

An id belonging to another tenant answers 404, not 403: the read runs against the verified tenant's database, so "does not exist" and "not yours" are the same answer and the response does not distinguish them.

`overrideName` on a line is OPERATOR-AUTHORED FREE TEXT and MAY CONTAIN PHI. `isCalculatedRate`, `invoiceIds` and the `null` location sentinel behave exactly as documented on `GET /v1/financials/estimates`.

Returns the tenant's invoices as a CHANGE FEED, one page at a time, ordered by `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)` ascending with the invoice id as a tie-break.

`modifiedDateUtc` carries that coalesced value and is therefore never null: the stored modified timestamp IS nullable and is null for every invoice nobody has edited, so an incremental consumer filtering on the raw column would never see them. Until the first edit, `modifiedDateUtc` equals `createdUtcDate`. The filter parameter is `updatedSince` while the response field is `modifiedDateUtc`; that asymmetry is deliberate and shared with the appointments public surface.

A LINE-ITEM edit moves the watermark. That is worth stating because it did not before this surface existed: the platform's line-item write paths wrote `InvoiceItems` and left the header alone, so a changed rate, quantity, discount or provider — money-affecting edits — would not have surfaced here. Those paths now stamp the parent invoice.

Filters: `updatedSince` (ISO-8601 timestamp, inclusive), `patientId`, `status` (repeatable — `status=Open&status=Paid` reads as OR), and `effectiveDateFrom` / `effectiveDateTo`, an inclusive range over the `effectiveDate` calendar date. `status` accepts exactly the values `/v1/financials/invoice-statuses` returns and rejects `Unknown`, which exists only to absorb a stored value from outside the contract on the way out.

Void and Deleted invoices ARE included by default and are returned with their status. Reporting consumers need to see reversals, and an invoice that disappeared from an incremental feed on being voided would leave a consumer holding a revenue figure it could never correct; narrow with `status` instead. There is no revision history in the schema — an edit overwrites the invoice and moves its watermark — so every row here is the current version of that invoice.

MONEY. The published header totals do NOT close on their own, and that is a property of the schema rather than an omission. The platform computes `amount` as `subTotalAmount - totalDiscount + the invoice's tax total`, and that tax total is the sum of the `InvoiceTaxes` breakdown rows, which this contract does not publish and no column stores. `coveredTaxesAmount` is a DIFFERENT figure — the tax the practice absorbs — and must not be substituted for it. `subTotalAmount` is itself GROSS of discount. `tipsTotal` and `surchargesTotal` are reported alongside `amount`, not inside it: tips accrue from payments, and the surcharge is a restatement of a line already present in `lineItems`, so adding either would double-count. Treat `amount` and `balanceDue` as authoritative and do not recompute them.

`paidAmount` is DERIVED as `amount - balanceDue`. It comes from the invoice's own maintained balance and is NOT a reconciliation against the payment ledger: no column stores it, and summing the payment allocations instead could disagree with the balance every other reader trusts. The payment x invoice split is intentionally not public, so a consumer needing payment-level detail reads the payments resource, which carries invoice ids without per-invoice amounts.

A cursor is bound to the filters it was issued under. Changing any filter value and replaying the cursor is rejected rather than silently resumed mid-stream in another patient's data.

Line items are INLINE, in `lineItems`, fetched set-based for the whole page. Note two things about them. `isCalculatedRate` says which arithmetic applies: when it is `false`, `subTotalAmount = rate × quantity − totalDiscount`; when it is `true`, `rate` IS the line total and that multiplication does not reconcile. `subTotalAmount` is authoritative either way. And `overrideName` is OPERATOR-AUTHORED FREE TEXT that MAY CONTAIN PHI — do not log it, cache it by it, or index it.

`estimateId` on the header names the estimate this invoice was raised from, if any; a line's `estimateItemId` names the estimate line it came from. Both point from invoice to estimate, which is the opposite of the estimate surface's `invoiceIds` — conversion is recorded on both sides but at different grains, so more than one invoice can name the same estimate.

`serviceLocationId` and `billingLocationId` are `null` when the practice never set them. The underlying columns are `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and 0 is a not-set sentinel rather than a location id, so publishing it would name a location that does not exist.

Not published: the tax breakdown, the per-payment allocation split, responsible-party payer splits (insurance is not in v1), memberships, certificates, Galderma posted items, and every operator free-text field other than `overrideName`.

`lineItems` IS BOUNDED. One page returns at most 25000 line rows in total across its invoices, and the single-invoice read is bounded the same way. The ceiling is orders of magnitude above any real invoice, so reaching it says something is wrong with the data rather than with the request. If it is ever reached the `lineItems` arrays on that page are truncated from the last invoice backwards — `next`, the paging keyset and the header fields are unaffected — and the service counts and logs the event rather than truncating in silence.

Returns one invoice with its line items inline — the same payload the collection returns, for a single id.

An id belonging to another tenant answers 404, not 403: the read runs against the verified tenant's database, so "does not exist" and "not yours" are the same answer and the response does not distinguish them.

`overrideName` on a line is OPERATOR-AUTHORED FREE TEXT and MAY CONTAIN PHI. The derivation of `paidAmount`, the fact that the header totals do not close without the unpublished tax total, `isCalculatedRate` and the `null` location sentinel all behave exactly as documented on `GET /v1/financials/invoices`.

Returns the tenant's credit notes as a CHANGE FEED, one page at a time, ordered by `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)` ascending with the credit note id as a tie-break.

`modifiedDateUtc` carries that coalesced value and is therefore never null: the stored modified timestamp IS nullable and is null for every credit note nobody has edited, so an incremental consumer filtering on the raw column would never see them. Until the first edit, `modifiedDateUtc` equals `createdUtcDate`. The filter parameter is `updatedSince` while the response field is `modifiedDateUtc`; that asymmetry is deliberate and shared with the appointments public surface.

`createdUtcDate` MAY BE `1900-01-01T00:00:00Z`. The column is `NOT NULL` with a `DEFAULT '1900-01-01'`, so a credit note written before the platform recorded creation timestamps carries that sentinel rather than a real date. Those rows are returned like any other — never skipped — but because the feed orders on the coalesced watermark, a sentinel-dated credit note that has also never been edited sits permanently at the FRONT of the feed. A consumer walking the feed from the beginning meets them first; one syncing on `updatedSince` never sees them again after the first pass.

Filters: `updatedSince` (ISO-8601 timestamp, inclusive), `patientId`, `status` (repeatable — `status=Open&status=Closed` reads as OR), and `effectiveDateFrom` / `effectiveDateTo`, an inclusive range over the `effectiveDate` calendar date. `status` accepts exactly the values `/v1/financials/credit-note-statuses` returns and rejects `Unknown`, which exists only to absorb a stored value from outside the contract on the way out.

`patientId` MAY BE NULL, and a credit note CAN EXIST WITHOUT A PATIENT. The underlying column is nullable — uniquely among invoices, estimates and credit notes — so a null there is the practice's data rather than a bug or a redaction. The consequence for paging is concrete: the `patientId` FILTER can never return such a credit note, so a consumer that syncs patient by patient will never see the unattributed ones and must page the unfiltered feed to reach them.

Void and Deleted credit notes ARE included by default and are returned with their status. A credit note is itself a reversal, and one that disappeared from an incremental feed on being voided would leave a consumer holding a credit the practice has since taken back; narrow with `status` instead. There is no revision history in the schema — an edit overwrites the credit note and moves its watermark — so every row here is the current version of that credit note.

MONEY. THERE IS NO TAX FIELD ON THIS PAYLOAD, and its absence is NOT an implicit zero. `CreditNotes` carries no tax column at all: no `taxTotal`, no `taxableSubTotalAmount`, no `nonTaxableSubTotalAmount` and — unlike the invoice and estimate payloads — not even `coveredTaxesAmount`. A taxed credit note's tax lives in the `CreditNoteTaxes` breakdown rows, which v1 drops, so the figure is UNAVAILABLE from this surface rather than zero. There is no `surchargesTotal` and no `tipsTotal` here either. `amount` is the credited total and is authoritative; `subTotalAmount` is GROSS of discount, so `subTotalAmount - totalDiscount` does not reach `amount` on a taxed credit note.

What DOES close is the four-way split of the credited total: `appliedAsPaymentAmount + refundedAmount + balance == amount`, reading each null as zero. That is a real invariant rather than an artefact of arithmetic — all four values are stored independently in their own columns — which is why it is worth relying on.

`appliedAsPaymentAmount` and `refundedAmount` are NULLABLE, and null does not mean zero. The platform sets both to null when the credit note has no live patient credit behind it, so "never applied" and "applied zero" are different facts and this contract keeps them apart rather than coalescing one into the other. `balance` is `NOT NULL` and reads 0 in that same case, so the two are not interchangeable.

A cursor is bound to the filters it was issued under. Changing any filter value and replaying the cursor is rejected rather than silently resumed mid-stream in another patient's data.

Line items are INLINE, in `lineItems`, fetched set-based for the whole page. Note three things about them. `isCalculatedRate` says which arithmetic applies: when it is `false`, `subTotalAmount = rate × quantity − totalDiscount`; when it is `true`, `rate` IS the line total and that multiplication does not reconcile. `subTotalAmount` is authoritative either way. `amountPaid` is per-LINE settlement and exists only on credit note lines — it is what makes per-line refund reconciliation possible, and unlike the header's applied and refunded figures it is never null. And `overrideName` is OPERATOR-AUTHORED FREE TEXT that MAY CONTAIN PHI — do not log it, cache it by it, or index it. It is NULLABLE on this line, where the same field on an invoice or estimate line is not.

`invoiceId` names the invoice this credit note was raised against, if any, and resolves through `GET /v1/financials/invoices/{id}`. `patientCreditId` is a REFERENCE ONLY: the patient-credit aggregate is not public in v1, so the id is not resolvable yet. It is published because it is the join key a consumer will need and because its presence distinguishes a credit note backed by a live patient credit from one that is not — the same distinction the two nullable money fields carry.

`serviceLocationId` and `billingLocationId` are `null` when the practice never set them. The underlying columns are `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and 0 is a not-set sentinel rather than a location id, so publishing it would name a location that does not exist.

Not published: every tax field and the `CreditNoteTaxes` breakdown, the nested patient-credit object and its applied-payment graph, memberships, CareCredit requests, the line's `isReturnable` inventory flag, and every operator free-text field other than `overrideName`. There are no `responsibleParties`: no such table exists for credit notes at all.

`lineItems` IS BOUNDED. One page returns at most 25000 line rows in total across its credit notes, and the single-credit-note read is bounded the same way. The ceiling is orders of magnitude above any real credit note, so reaching it says something is wrong with the data rather than with the request. If it is ever reached the `lineItems` arrays on that page are truncated from the last credit note backwards — `next`, the paging keyset and the header fields are unaffected — and the service counts and logs the event rather than truncating in silence.

Returns one credit note with its line items inline — the same payload the collection returns, for a single id.

An id belonging to another tenant answers 404, not 403: the read runs against the verified tenant's database, so "does not exist" and "not yours" are the same answer and the response does not distinguish them. Note that `Deleted` is a real, returned status on this resource, so a 404 here never means "deleted".

`overrideName` on a line is OPERATOR-AUTHORED FREE TEXT, MAY CONTAIN PHI, and is nullable. The absence of every tax field, the nullable `patientId`, the nullable `appliedAsPaymentAmount` / `refundedAmount` and their invariant with `balance` and `amount`, the `1900-01-01` creation sentinel, `isCalculatedRate` and the `null` location sentinel all behave exactly as documented on `GET /v1/financials/credit-notes`.

Returns the tenant's payments as a CHANGE FEED, one page at a time, ordered by `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)` ascending with the payment id as a tie-break.

`modifiedDateUtc` carries that coalesced value and is therefore never null: the stored modified timestamp IS nullable and is null for every payment nobody has deleted, voided or re-shared — which is nearly all of them — so an incremental consumer filtering on the raw column would see almost nothing. Until the first edit, `modifiedDateUtc` equals `createdUtcDate`. The filter parameter is `updatedSince` while the response field is `modifiedDateUtc`; that asymmetry is deliberate and shared with the appointments public surface.

REVENUE BUCKETING. Daily collected revenue per location and per payment method is reconstructable from this feed alone: bucket on `paymentDate` (the calendar date the practice recorded the payment against), `locationId` and `paymentMode.paymentType`, and sum `amount`. Use `paymentMode.paymentType` and NOT `paymentMode.name` or `paymentMode.id` — the name is practice-renamable and the id is tenant-local, so neither is comparable across tenants or stable over time; the type is the only cross-tenant-stable classification and it is mandatory on every payment. Two things to get right: `isRefund` carries the DIRECTION, because `amount` is not signed, so subtract refunds rather than expecting the signs to cancel; and narrow with `status=Active` unless you want the deleted and voided rows, which this feed returns by default.

Filters: `updatedSince` (ISO-8601 timestamp, inclusive), `patientId`, `status` (repeatable — `status=Deleted&status=Voided` reads as OR), and `paymentDateFrom` / `paymentDateTo`, an inclusive range over the `paymentDate` calendar date. `status` accepts exactly the values `/v1/financials/payment-statuses` returns. There is deliberately no `locationId` filter in v1: no index covers that column, so bucket by `locationId` client-side from the page.

`status` IS SYNTHESIZED and no column holds it. It is derived from two internal flags that are NOT exposed, `IsDeleted` and `IsVoided`, which are independent — so BOTH CAN BE TRUE ON ONE PAYMENT. When they are, the status reads `Deleted`: deletion is the more terminal fact, and if voiding won instead, a consumer excluding deleted payments would meet the same payment again as a voided one. So the three values PARTITION the collection, and `Voided` means voided AND NOT deleted.

Deleted and voided payments ARE included by default and are returned with their status. A payment that vanished from an incremental feed on being voided would leave a reporting consumer counting revenue the practice has since reversed; narrow with `status` instead. There is no revision history in the schema — an edit overwrites the payment — so every row here is the current version of that payment.

`patientId` MAY BE NULL, and A PAYMENT CAN EXIST WITHOUT A PATIENT. The underlying column is nullable, and the case that produces it is an INSURANCE PAYMENT: such a payment carries an insurance company instead of a patient, and that id is NOT published in v1. So when `patientId` is null, THIS CONTRACT CANNOT TELL YOU WHOSE PAYMENT IT IS — nothing else on the payload identifies the payer. It is the practice's data rather than a bug or a redaction. The consequence for paging is concrete: the `patientId` FILTER can never return such a payment, so a consumer that syncs patient by patient will never see the insurance payments and must page the unfiltered feed to reach them.

MONEY. `amount` is the gross figure the practice took, INCLUSIVE of `surchargeAmount` and of any tip — and tips are not published, so `amount - surchargeAmount` is not the invoice-applied total either. `surchargeAmount` is NULLABLE and null does not mean zero: the column is nullable and "no surcharge" and "a surcharge of zero" are different facts, so this contract keeps them apart rather than coalescing one into the other. There is no tips total, no per-invoice split and no patient-credit breakdown on this payload.

`invoiceIds` carries REFERENCES ONLY and MAY BE EMPTY. The per-allocation amount exists in the schema and is deliberately not published: the split of one payment across several invoices is not part of the public contract, and per-invoice reconciliation is done from the invoice side through `invoice.paidAmount`. Soft-deleted allocations are EXCLUDED, so an invoice a payment was unlinked from does not appear — without that filter a payment would keep advertising a link it no longer has, and since the amount is not published there would be no second signal to notice it from. An empty array is a real state, e.g. a patient-credit payment, and it does not mean the payment was deleted.

`creditCardType` is a SCALAR, not a nested object, and it is `null` for every payment with no credit-card row — cash, check, patient credit, gift card, rewards. `Unknown` is a REAL RETURNED VALUE on this field, unlike the `Unknown` on the status enums: it means the brand was not recorded. So `null` means "not a card payment" and `Unknown` means "a card payment whose brand nobody recorded". No cardholder name, card reference, vault id, gateway, processor, merchant id, terminal id, token or authorization code exists anywhere in this contract.

`locationId` is NEVER NULL here, and that differs from the invoice, estimate and credit-note payloads: their location columns are `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and publish `null` for the 0 not-set sentinel, while `Payments.LocationID` has no default and always names a real location.

A cursor is bound to the filters it was issued under. Changing any filter value and replaying the cursor is rejected rather than silently resumed mid-stream in another patient's data.

Not published: the internal `isDeleted` and `isVoided` flags that `status` replaces, the insurance company, the destination account, the payment request, the recurring payment, the payment draft, the transaction reference, `sharedWithPatient`, the created and modified user ids, the tips, the patient credits and applied patient credits, the gift card payments, the rewards payment and its third-party loyalty member reference, the CareCredit requests, the refund history, and the operator free text `notes`, `voidedReason` and `deletedReason`.

`invoiceIds` IS BOUNDED, and so is the read behind `creditCardType`. One page returns at most 25000 invoice links in total across its payments, and at most that many card rows, and the single-payment read is bounded the same way. Both ceilings are orders of magnitude above any real payment, so reaching either says something is wrong with the data rather than with the request. If one is ever reached the affected values on that page are truncated from the last payment backwards — `next`, the paging keyset and every other field are unaffected — and the service counts and logs the event rather than truncating in silence.

Returns one payment — the same payload the collection returns, for a single id.

An id belonging to another tenant answers 404, not 403: the read runs against the verified tenant's database, so "does not exist" and "not yours" are the same answer and the response does not distinguish them. Note that `Deleted` is a real, returned status on this resource, so a 404 here never means "deleted".

The synthesized `status` and its `Deleted`-over-`Voided` precedence, the nullable `patientId` and the insurance payment behind it, the nullable `surchargeAmount`, the nullable `paymentReason`, the scalar `creditCardType` and its two distinct absent states, and the reference-only `invoiceIds` with soft-deleted allocations excluded all behave exactly as documented on `GET /v1/financials/payments`.

Returns the tenant's membership programmes as a CHANGE FEED, one page at a time, ordered by `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)` ascending with the programme id as a tie-break.

`modifiedDateUtc` carries that coalesced value and is therefore never null: the stored modified timestamp IS nullable and is null for every programme nobody has edited since the audit columns were added, so an incremental consumer filtering on the raw column would see nothing. Until the first edit, `modifiedDateUtc` equals `createdUtcDate`. The filter parameter is `updatedSince` while the response field is `modifiedDateUtc`; that asymmetry is deliberate and platform-wide.

A DELETED PROGRAMME IS INVISIBLE ON THIS FEED, AND YOU CANNOT DETECT IT FROM HERE. Deletion on this table is a HARD DELETE and the table has no `IsDeleted` column, so no row survives to carry a watermark and there is nothing for a change feed to report — the programme simply stops appearing. This is the one acknowledged hole in the incremental guarantee on this API. A consumer that must notice removals has to reconcile against a full unfiltered page rather than relying on `updatedSince`. The same fact is why a membership's `membershipProgramId` can outlive the programme it names and answer 404 on `/v1/financials/membership-programs/{id}`.

Filters: `updatedSince` (ISO-8601 timestamp, inclusive) and `status` (repeatable, though with two values repeating it is the same as omitting it). `status` accepts exactly the values `/v1/financials/membership-program-statuses` returns.

`status` IS SYNTHESIZED and no column holds it. `Active` means AVAILABLE FOR ENROLMENT: the practice has the programme switched on AND today falls inside the `startDate` … `endDate` window, both bounds inclusive, judged by UTC calendar date. `Inactive` is the exact negation — switched off, not started yet, or already ended — so the two values partition the collection and you can recompute both from this payload, except for the switch itself: the stored `IsEnabled` flag is NOT published, so an `Inactive` programme whose dates look current is one the practice has turned off.

Disabled and ended programmes ARE included by default and are returned with their status, because a membership enrolled years ago still points at its programme and a consumer resolving that reference needs the row to exist. Narrow with `status=Active` for the current catalogue.

`duration` HAS NO RECORDED UNIT AND THIS SERVICE NEVER USES IT. There is no expiration arithmetic anywhere in the financials service: a membership's `expirationDate` is a stored column set by whoever enrolled the patient, not computed from this number. Treat `duration` as descriptive metadata the practice configured — display it, do not compute an expiry from it. A membership's own `expirationDate` on `/v1/financials/memberships` is the authoritative answer.

`itemId` IS NULLABLE and the null is a real state: a programme can be configured without a catalog item. It is a REFERENCE ONLY — the item is never joined, so no item name or price appears here. `giftCardAmount` is nullable on the same terms as any money column on this surface: null means the programme grants no gift card, which is not the same fact as granting one worth zero.

DATES. `startDate` and `endDate` are stored in `DATETIME` columns rather than `DATE` ones and are published as CALENDAR DATES: the time part is not published and plays no part in `status`, so the window you read and the status you read are computed from the same values. `createdUtcDate` is different in a way worth stating: for every programme that existed before the audit columns were added it is THE TIMESTAMP THE COLUMN WAS ADDED, not a real creation date — there was nothing to backfill it from — so a whole practice's programmes commonly share one value unrelated to when they were configured. Use `startDate` for when the offering began.

A cursor is bound to the filters it was issued under. Changing any filter value and replaying the cursor is rejected rather than silently resumed.

Not published: the whole `discounts[]` collection and the three obsolete discount triples — the enums that said what a discount applied to and whether its amount was a rate or a sum are all out of v1, and a discount without its target is not interpretable; `type` and `applicationType`, both obsolete; `isCombineEnabled`; `partnerId` and the partner extended information; `iconId`, because media is v2; the `isEnabled` flag that `status` replaces; and the nested catalog item.

Returns one membership programme — the same payload the collection returns, for a single id.

An id belonging to another tenant answers 404, not 403: the read runs against the verified tenant's database, so "does not exist" and "not yours" are the same answer and the response does not distinguish them. A THIRD case answers 404 here and is worth knowing about: a programme that was DELETED. Deletion on this table is a hard delete with no `IsDeleted` column, so a membership's `membershipProgramId` can outlive the programme it names, and this endpoint cannot tell you which of the three happened.

The synthesized `status` and its availability window, the unit-less `duration`, the nullable `itemId` and `giftCardAmount`, and the `createdUtcDate` caveat for pre-migration rows all behave exactly as documented on `GET /v1/financials/membership-programs`.

Returns the tenant's patient memberships as a CHANGE FEED, one page at a time, ordered by `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)` ascending with the membership id as a tie-break.

`modifiedDateUtc` carries that coalesced value and is therefore never null: the stored modified timestamp IS nullable and is null for every membership nobody has cancelled, extended or paid for since the audit columns were added — which is nearly all of them — so an incremental consumer filtering on the raw column would see almost nothing. Until the first edit, `modifiedDateUtc` equals `createdUtcDate`. The filter parameter is `updatedSince` while the response field is `modifiedDateUtc`; that asymmetry is deliberate and shared with the appointments public surface.

Filters: `updatedSince` (ISO-8601 timestamp, inclusive), `patientId`, `status` (repeatable — `status=Expired&status=Cancelled` reads as OR), and `startDateFrom` / `startDateTo`, an inclusive range over the `startDate` calendar date. `status` accepts exactly the values `/v1/financials/membership-statuses` returns.

`status` IS SYNTHESIZED and no column holds it. THREE of the four values are produced, and they partition the collection in this precedence — `Cancelled`, then `Expired`, then `Active`:

- `Cancelled` — the membership was cancelled, whatever its dates say. Identical to `isCancelled: true`, which is published beside it.
- `Expired` — `expirationDate` is set and is BEFORE TODAY. A NULL `expirationDate` never expires, and that is a common state rather than missing data.
- `Active` — neither of the above.

`Past` IS RESERVED AND THIS FEED NEVER RETURNS IT. `/v1/financials/membership-statuses` still lists it, and `?status=Past` is accepted and matches nothing. The value means "superseded by a later membership", which can only be derived from a DIFFERENT row — and enrolling a patient again does not modify the membership it supersedes, so `modifiedDateUtc` on the older row would not move. An incremental reader polling `updatedSince` would receive the new membership and never be told the old one had stopped being current, leaving the patient holding two `Active` memberships in your store with nothing in the feed to reveal it. `Cancelled` and `Expired` are safe precisely because you can recompute them from a payload you already hold; supersession cannot be. IF YOU NEED IT: group the collection by `patientId` and `membershipProgramId` and order by `startDate` — every field that requires is published.

TWO THINGS ABOUT `Active` THAT A CONSUMER MUST NOT ASSUME AWAY. First, IT INCLUDES A MEMBERSHIP THAT HAS NOT STARTED YET: `startDate` plays no part in the rule, because the published vocabulary has no "pending" value to give instead, so a membership enrolled today to begin next month reads `Active`. If you mean "in force today", compare `startDate` yourself — it is published for exactly that.

Second, THIS CONTRACT'S `status` DELIBERATELY DISAGREES WITH THE PRACTICE-FACING MEMBERSHIP REPORT for one population. That report treats any membership in a PARTNER programme as active regardless of its dates or its cancellation. `membershipProgram.type` and `partnerId` are NOT published in v1, so honouring that rule here would return `Active` on a membership whose published dates say otherwise, with nothing on the payload to explain it. Every value this feed returns is computed only from fields it publishes, so you can always recompute it; where a practice's own report differs for a partner programme, that is why.

Cancelled memberships ARE included by default and are returned with their status. One that vanished from an incremental feed on being cancelled would leave a consumer granting a benefit the practice has since withdrawn; narrow with `status` instead. There is no revision history in the schema — an edit overwrites the membership — so every row here is the current version.

`membershipProgramId` IS A REFERENCE AND NOT PROOF THE PROGRAMME IS AVAILABLE. The foreign key guarantees the id named a row when the membership was written, and nothing more: that programme may be disabled, may have ended, and may since have been HARD-DELETED — in which case `/v1/financials/membership-programs/{id}` answers 404 while this id still points at it. Resolve it there if you need its state.

`invoiceId` and `giftCardId` are REFERENCES ONLY and both are nullable. Resolve them through `/v1/financials/invoices/{id}` and `/v1/financials/gift-cards/{id}`; no gift card NUMBER is published here or even read.

DATES. `startDate` and `expirationDate` are stored in `DATETIME` columns rather than `DATE` ones and are published as CALENDAR DATES: the time part is not published and plays no part in `status`, which is evaluated by UTC calendar date, so the dates you read and the status you read are computed from the same values. `assignedDateUtc` is different — it genuinely is an instant, set from the server clock when the enrolment was recorded.

`createdUtcDate` EQUALS `assignedDateUtc` EXACTLY for every membership enrolled before the audit columns were added, because it was backfilled from it. Do not read significance into the two agreeing on a historical row; they are the same number.

A cursor is bound to the filters it was issued under. Changing any filter value and replaying the cursor is rejected rather than silently resumed mid-stream in another patient's data.

Not published: the nested membership programme, gift card and invoice objects (ids only), the gift card number, and the programme's own fields — its name, price, duration and availability window all live on `/v1/financials/membership-programs`.

Returns one membership — the same payload the collection returns, for a single id.

An id belonging to another tenant answers 404, not 403: the read runs against the verified tenant's database, so "does not exist" and "not yours" are the same answer and the response does not distinguish them. Note that `Cancelled` is a real, returned status on this resource, so a 404 here never means "cancelled".

The synthesized `status` and its `Cancelled`-`Expired`-`Active` precedence, the fact that `Active` includes a membership that has not started yet, the deliberate disagreement with the practice-facing report over partner programmes, and the reference-only `membershipProgramId`, `invoiceId` and `giftCardId` all behave exactly as documented on `GET /v1/financials/memberships`.

Returns the tenant's gift cards as a CHANGE FEED, one page at a time, ordered by `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)` ascending with the gift card id as a tie-break.

`modifiedDateUtc` carries that coalesced value and is therefore never null: the stored modified timestamp IS nullable and is null for every card nobody has edited, deleted, funded or spent, so an incremental consumer filtering on the raw column would miss a large population. Until the first change, `modifiedDateUtc` equals `createdUtcDate`. The filter parameter is `updatedSince` while the response field is `modifiedDateUtc`; that asymmetry is deliberate and shared with the appointments public surface.

IT MOVES WHEN THE BALANCE MOVES. Funding a card, spending it, and reversing either are changes to the card's payment ledger rather than to the card row, and each one is deliberately stamped onto the card's watermark — so `value` and the `Redeemed` status are safe to sync on incrementally, which is the whole reason they are published.

Filters: `updatedSince` (ISO-8601 timestamp, inclusive), `status` (repeatable — `status=Active&status=Expired` reads as OR), and `issuedDateFrom` / `issuedDateTo`, an inclusive range over the `issuedDate` calendar date. `status` accepts exactly the values `/v1/financials/gift-card-statuses` returns.

THERE IS NO `locationId` FILTER ON THIS RESOURCE, and that is a deliberate subtraction rather than an omission: `GiftCards` HAS NO LOCATION COLUMN and there is no join that would produce one. A location appears only on the payment that funds or spends a card, which is a property of that payment and not of the card — a card can be funded at one location and spent at another. If you need to attribute gift card activity to a location, read `/v1/financials/payments` and filter there.

THERE IS ALSO NO `patientId` FILTER, for a different reason: a gift card has TWO patients — `purchaserPatientId` and `holderPatientId` — so a single `patientId` filter would have to pick one meaning or silently OR them together, and the internal equivalent mixes both with a permission rule this contract does not have. Both ids are published on every card, so filter client-side; if a server-side filter is added later it will be additive.

`cardNumber` IS MASKED and never returned in full — a gift card number is a redeemable instrument. The rule is length-aware, because the column has no length constraint: a number of 9 characters or more keeps its first 4 and last 4, one of 5 to 8 keeps only its last 4, and one of 4 CHARACTERS OR FEWER KEEPS NOTHING. Hidden characters are replaced one-for-one with `*`, so the length of the original is preserved and the value is unmistakably a mask.

`value` AND `maxValue` ARE DIFFERENT FACTS and this is the single most likely misreading of this payload. `value` is the REMAINING BALANCE, derived from the card's signed payment ledger; `maxValue` is the FACE VALUE it was issued for, stored, and NULLABLE — a null means the card has no stated maximum, which is not the same as zero. A card issued for 100 and never funded reads `value: 0, maxValue: 100` and `status: Draft`; a fully spent one reads `value: 0, maxValue: 100` and `status: Redeemed`. The balance can go UP as well as down, because a reversed redemption returns it.

`status` IS ONE MERGED FIELD: the stored status and the computed processing status are not both exposed. Three values are stored and TAKE PRECEDENCE — a `Draft` or `Deleted` card reads that way whatever its dates and its balance say — and two are derived on read:

- `Draft` — created, not issued. Usually unfunded, so usually `value: 0`.
- `Deleted` — removed by the practice. A REAL, RETURNED status: this table has no delete flag, deletion IS this value, and deleted cards stay in the feed with it.
- `Redeemed` — issued and fully spent: the ledger has at least one live entry and the entries sum to zero. An UNFUNDED card is NOT `Redeemed`, even though its balance is also zero — nothing was ever spent, so it reads `Active`.
- `Expired` — issued, not spent out, and `expirationDate` is set and is TODAY OR EARLIER. The bound is INCLUSIVE. A NULL `expirationDate` never expires, and that is a common state rather than missing data.
- `Active` — issued and none of the above.

`Redeemed` BEATS `Expired`: a card spent out that has also passed its expiration date reads `Redeemed`. Both derived values are computed only from fields this payload publishes, so you can always recompute them.

`availabilityDate` PLAYS NO PART IN `status`. A card whose availability date is in the future reads `Active` even though the practice cannot spend it yet, because the published vocabulary has no value for "issued but not yet usable". Compare that date yourself if you mean "spendable today".

Deleted cards ARE included by default and are returned with their status. One that vanished from an incremental feed on being deleted would leave a consumer honouring a balance the practice has since withdrawn and refunded; narrow with `status` instead. There is no revision history in the schema — an edit overwrites the card — so every row here is the current version.

`description` IS OPERATOR-AUTHORED FREE TEXT AND MAY CONTAIN PHI. A practice can type anything into it, including a patient's name or a procedure. It is one of only two free-text fields on this whole surface, it ships because a gift card is meaningless to a practice without the note explaining it, and it is your responsibility downstream: do not log it, do not index it for search, and do not display it outside an authorized clinical or billing context.

DATES. `issuedDate`, `availabilityDate` and `expirationDate` are stored in real `DATE` columns and are published as CALENDAR DATES with NO `Utc` suffix — there is no time part and no timezone to assert. `createdUtcDate` and `modifiedDateUtc` are `DATETIME` columns holding genuine instants and keep theirs. The status rule is evaluated by UTC calendar date, so the dates you read and the status you read are computed from the same values.

`occasion` IS NEVER NULL: `OccasionId` is `NOT NULL` with a foreign key. Its id is tenant-local for anything a practice created, and its name is practice-renamable — show the name, group on nothing. An id of `0` is NOT a not-set sentinel: it is the platform-seeded `Other` occasion. The occasion may since have been deactivated or deleted by the practice; `/v1/financials/gift-card-occasions` carries those flags.

A cursor is bound to the filters it was issued under. Changing any filter value and replaying the cursor is rejected rather than silently resumed mid-stream.

Not published: the full card number, the purchaser's and holder's NAMES (ids only), the card's payment ledger as a collection, and the users who created or last modified the card. Redemption shows up on `/v1/financials/payments`.

Returns one gift card — the same payload the collection returns, for a single id.

An id belonging to another tenant answers 404, not 403: the read runs against the verified tenant's database, so "does not exist" and "not yours" are the same answer and the response does not distinguish them. Note that `Deleted` is a real, returned status on this resource, so a 404 here never means "deleted" — a deleted card is fetchable and reads `status: Deleted`.

The masked `cardNumber`, the difference between `value` and `maxValue`, the merged `status` with its stored-first precedence and its inclusive expiry bound, and the free-text `description` all behave exactly as documented on `GET /v1/financials/gift-cards`.

Returns the tenant's catalog items as a CHANGE FEED, one page at a time, ordered by `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)` ascending with the item id as a tie-break.

`modifiedDateUtc` carries that coalesced value and is therefore never null: the stored modified timestamp IS nullable and is null for every item nobody has edited since it was created, so an incremental consumer filtering on the raw column would miss a large population. Until the first change, `modifiedDateUtc` equals `createdUtcDate`. The filter parameter is `updatedSince` while the response field is `modifiedDateUtc`; that asymmetry is deliberate and shared with the appointments public surface.

THERE IS NO `isActive` FILTER, AND NO `isActive` FIELD, because `Items` HAS NO SUCH COLUMN. It has THREE INDEPENDENT FLAGS and conflating them is the single most likely mistake against this resource:

- `isForSale` — a stored boolean, and THE ONE THE PRACTICE'S ACTIVE/INACTIVE TOGGLE WRITES. If you want "is the practice currently selling this", this is the field, and it is the only one of the three you can filter on.
- `status` — a NAME joined from a separate lookup table, seeded `NotSet`, `Active`, `Inactive` and `Backordered`. THE TOGGLE NEVER TOUCHES IT, so an item that reads `status: "Active"` and `isForSale: false` is not inconsistent — that is the ordinary state of an item a practice has stopped selling without editing its status. The lookup table is not constrained, so a practice's own value can appear and this is NOT a closed vocabulary; there is no status lookup endpoint and no `status` filter, so do not switch on the string.
- `isDeleted` — a SOFT DELETE, and orthogonal to both. Deleting an item sets this flag and leaves `isForSale` and `status` exactly as they were, so a deleted item can read `isForSale: true`.

A DELETED ITEM AND AN INACTIVE ITEM ARE DIFFERENT THINGS. An inactive item — whether that means `isForSale: false` or `status: "Inactive"` — is a live catalog entry the practice is not selling right now and can start selling again; it still appears in pickers that ask for it and it is still editable. A deleted item has been withdrawn: it is hidden from every internal read by default and is not meant to be sold again. Neither one is removed from the database, and NEITHER IS FILTERED OUT OF THIS FEED — deleted and inactive items are returned with their flags set, because an item that vanished from an incremental feed would leave a consumer holding a catalog entry it can never retire, and every invoice, estimate and credit-note line ever written against it still names it.

Filters: `updatedSince` (ISO-8601 timestamp, inclusive), `isForSale` (exactly `true` or `false`), and `createdFrom` / `createdTo`, an INCLUSIVE range over the calendar date of `createdUtcDate`. Note that `createdUtcDate` is a genuine timestamp rather than a date column, so `createdTo` includes the WHOLE of the day you name, in UTC.

THERE IS NO `categoryId` FILTER AND NO `itemGroupId` FILTER. Both were considered and both are left out of v1 deliberately; adding either later is additive, so the omission is the cheap direction. `categories[]` is on every item, so filtering by category client-side works today at the cost of reading the catalog. If you need one of these server-side, ask — `categoryId` is the one that would come first, because the junction table's clustered key leads with the category id and would support it as a seek, whereas nothing indexes the item-group side at all.

THERE IS NO `locationId` FILTER either. `Items` is global to the tenant: an item has no location, and what a location owns is a PRICE and an inventory level for it — both of which are out of v1.

`flatPrice` IS THE GLOBAL LIST PRICE AND NOT WHAT ANYONE PAYS. Three things override it and none is published in v1: a per-location price, a tiered schedule keyed on quantity and location, and any discount applied on the document. The price actually charged lives on the invoice line — read `/v1/financials/invoices` or `/v1/financials/estimates`. A null `flatPrice` is a real state meaning the item is priced elsewhere, NOT a price of zero.

`status`, `unit` AND `gender` ARE FLAT STRINGS with no id and no reference object, because the three tables behind them are not part of this surface — an id here would be a key with nothing to resolve it against. A null `gender` is the common case and means the item has NO gender restriction, not that the value is unknown.

`brand` AND `itemType` ARE NEVER NULL, both being `NOT NULL` columns with foreign keys. Note that the brand's NOT-SET VALUE IS A NAME, NOT AN ID: the platform seeds `Unknown` and `None` as real brands, so do not read a brand id of `0` as unset, and do not collapse `Unknown` to null — `Unknown` and `None` mean different things.

`categories[]` IS A MANY-TO-MANY and is fetched set-based for the whole page, so one page costs one query for the items and one for their category links regardless of page size. It is INDEPENDENT of `hierarchicalCategory`, which is a different, single-parent taxonomy: an item can be in both, either or neither, and the two are not views of the same data.

TWO CHANGES DO NOT MOVE `modifiedDateUtc`, and both are schema-level cascades no application code sees. Deleting a `Category` is a HARD delete and `ItemCategories` cascades with it, so the category silently disappears from every item that carried it with no watermark moving. Deleting a hierarchical category is normally a SOFT delete, which leaves the item pointing at a deleted category — resolve the id against `/v1/financials/item-hierarchical-categories`, which publishes `isDeleted`, rather than assuming a named category is live. If a hierarchical category is ever hard-deleted, the item's reference is nulled by the foreign key's `ON DELETE SET NULL` action, again with no watermark movement. Re-assigning an item's categories through the API DOES move the watermark. If you depend on the taxonomy, re-read `/v1/financials/item-categories` and `/v1/financials/item-hierarchical-categories` periodically rather than trusting this feed alone.

`hierarchicalCategory.parentId` IS NOT PROOF THE PARENT IS LIVE, and not proof it exists: that column has NO foreign key at all, and the internal write path validates a parent without checking whether it is deleted, so a live category can sit under a soft-deleted one.

`description` is OPERATOR-AUTHORED but is CATALOG PRODUCT COPY, not a patient note: it describes the service or product and lives on a row shared by every patient ever billed for the item, so it is not treated as PHI and ships unconditionally.

A cursor is bound to the filters it was issued under. Changing any filter value and replaying the cursor is rejected rather than silently resumed mid-stream.

Not published: cost of goods, purchase info and margin; pictures; CPT and insurance coding; inventory of any kind, global or per location; price schedules and per-location prices; the inventory-tracking, price-type and parent/child-type enums; the third-party `apxId` and Galderma product id; the base item id; the sales account id; and the users who created or last modified the item.

`categories` IS BOUNDED. One page returns at most 25000 category links in total across its items, and the single-item read is bounded the same way. The ceiling is orders of magnitude above any real item, so reaching it says something is wrong with the data rather than with the request. If it is ever reached the `categories` arrays on that page are truncated from the last item backwards — `next`, the paging keyset and every other field are unaffected — and the service counts and logs the event rather than truncating in silence.

Returns one catalog item — the same payload the collection returns, for a single id.

An id belonging to another tenant answers 404, not 403: the read runs against the verified tenant's database, so "does not exist" and "not yours" are the same answer and the response does not distinguish them. A DELETED ITEM IS STILL FETCHABLE and returns `isDeleted: true`, so a 404 here never means "deleted".

The three independent availability flags, the list-price-only `flatPrice`, the flat `status` / `unit` / `gender` strings, the never-null `brand` with its name-shaped not-set value, and the two taxonomy fields with their unstamped cascades all behave exactly as documented on `GET /v1/financials/items`.

Returns the tenant's item groups as a CHANGE FEED, one page at a time, ordered by `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)` ascending with the item group id as a tie-break. An item group is a named bundle of catalog items a practice can add to a document in one action.

`modifiedDateUtc` carries that coalesced value and is therefore never null; until the first change it equals `createdUtcDate`. The filter parameter is `updatedSince` while the response field is `modifiedDateUtc`, an asymmetry that is deliberate and platform-wide.

IT MOVES WHEN A MEMBER ITEM MOVES. `details[]` ships inline, so adding, changing or removing a member is a change to a child row rather than to the group — and each one is deliberately stamped onto the group's watermark, including the cascade that fires when the underlying catalog item is deleted. So `details[]` is safe to sync on incrementally, which is the whole reason it is published inline rather than as a separate resource.

THERE ARE NO MONEY AMOUNTS ON THIS RESOURCE, and that is a deliberate subtraction rather than an omission — the internal equivalent of this payload carries a subtotal, a discount and a total, and this one does not. `ItemGroups` HAS NO MONEY COLUMN AT ALL, so any amount would have to be computed, and the computation cannot be stated in terms of what this contract publishes:

- IT DEPENDS ON A LOCATION. The same group has a different total at every location, because a per-location price overrides the item's global one. There is no location on this resource and none on `/v1/financials/items`, so there is no location for an answer to be relative to.
- IT DEPENDS ON TIERED PRICING. When a member item is priced per tier, its contribution comes from a price schedule keyed on quantity and location. Price schedules are out of v1.
- IT DEPENDS ON A PER-MEMBER DISCOUNT KIND that is out of v1 too. A member can carry a fixed discount, a percentage discount, or neither, and WHICH ONE IT CARRIES CHANGES WHICH ARITHMETIC APPLIES — including whether the member's price comes from the group or from the item. That kind is an enum this contract does not publish.

So a total published here would be a number you could not check and could not reproduce. Worse, it would go stale silently: its inputs live on the item and its price schedules, and editing an item's price does NOT move this group's `modifiedDateUtc`, so an incremental consumer would hold a wrong total forever with nothing in this feed to reveal it. Publishing them later is additive; publishing a guessed one is not reversible. If you need a group's price, read the member items from `/v1/financials/items` and apply your own rule, or read the invoice or estimate the group was actually added to — which carries the price that was really charged.

THERE IS NO `isForSale` FIELD either, for the same reason: it is not a column on the group. The internal equivalent derives it from whether EVERY member item is for sale, which reads a value off the items — so it too would change without this feed saying anything. `/v1/financials/items` publishes `isForSale` per item and `details[]` gives you the member ids; intersect the two.

Filters: `updatedSince` (ISO-8601 timestamp, inclusive) and `isActive` (exactly `true` or `false`).

`isActive` IS A REAL STORED COLUMN HERE, unlike on `/v1/financials/items`, where the same word has no column behind it. It is INDEPENDENT of `isDeleted`: deleting a group does not clear it, so a deleted group can read `isActive: true`. Deleted and inactive groups are both RETURNED, carrying their flags — one that vanished from an incremental feed would leave a consumer offering a package the practice has withdrawn. Narrow with `isActive`; for deletion, read the flag.

`details[]` CARRIES TWO FIELDS PER MEMBER, `itemId` and `quantity`, and is fetched set-based for the whole page. A null `quantity` is a real stored state meaning none was ever set, which is not the same as a quantity of zero. A GROUP CAN NAME A DELETED ITEM — item deletion is soft and cascades to nothing here — so read the item on `/v1/financials/items` and check its `isDeleted` rather than assuming every member is live. The member's price, discount and discount kind are not published, for the reasons above. An empty `details[]` is a real state: nothing requires a group to contain anything.

A cursor is bound to the filters it was issued under. Changing either filter value and replaying the cursor is rejected rather than silently resumed mid-stream.

Not published: the three money amounts and their currency, `isForSale`, each member's price, discount and discount kind, the member row's own id, and the practice's favourite and recent-group lists.

`details` IS BOUNDED. One page returns at most 25000 detail rows in total across its groups, and the single-group read is bounded the same way. The ceiling is orders of magnitude above any real group, so reaching it says something is wrong with the data rather than with the request. Truncation matters more here than elsewhere, because `details` is what a group IS: a truncated one describes a smaller bundle rather than an incomplete list. So if the ceiling is ever reached — the arrays are truncated from the last group backwards, `next` and the paging keyset unaffected — the service counts and logs it rather than answering in silence.

Returns one item group — the same payload the collection returns, for a single id.

An id belonging to another tenant answers 404, not 403: the read runs against the verified tenant's database, so "does not exist" and "not yours" are the same answer. A DELETED GROUP IS STILL FETCHABLE and returns `isDeleted: true`, so a 404 here never means "deleted".

The absent money amounts, the absent `isForSale`, the independence of `isActive` and `isDeleted`, and the inline `details[]` with its nullable quantity all behave exactly as documented on `GET /v1/financials/item-groups`.

id.description: Gets the brand id.

name.description: Gets the name. This is the column's name and the field name on the wire.

isDeleted.description:
Gets a value indicating whether the brand has been removed by the practice. Deleted brands stay in
this lookup because historical items still reference them; a consumer that only wants the currently
selectable brands filters on this field.

PublicBrand.description:
A brand: the practice-configurable list the inline `brand` reference on an item points at.
Property order is the wire order, and it is the field set PLA-1067 published — nothing more.

id.description: Gets the brand id. Tenant-local, and resolvable through `/v1/financials/item-brands`.

name.description: Gets the brand's name. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL`, and practice-renamable.

PublicBrandReference.description:
A brand, as it appears inline on an item. Two fields only; `/v1/financials/item-brands` carries the
    `isDeleted` flag.
    NEVER NULL. Items.BrandID is INT NOT NULL with a foreign key, so every item has one — and
THE NOT-SET SENTINEL HERE IS A NAME RATHER THAN AN ID. Brands is seeded (1,'Unknown') and
(2,'None'), so an item whose brand is unrecorded still points at a real row with a real id. Do not
read an id of 0 as "unset" — that convention belongs to the invoice and estimate aggregates, not
here — and do not translate 'Unknown' into null: the two seeded names mean different things
("nobody said" versus "deliberately none") and collapsing either loses that.

id.description: Gets the category id. This is the value one of an item's `categories[].id` refers to.

name.description:
Gets the name. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL` per the DACPAC, so this is `required` rather than
nullable.

PublicCategory.description:
A category: the practice-configurable list an item's `categories[]` entries point at.
    Property order is the wire order, and it is the whole table — Categories has exactly two columns,
CategoryID and Name, and both are published.
    This is the flat category list, not the hierarchical one: HierarchicalCategories is a separate
table with its own parentId and its own delete flag, served by its own lookup.

id.description: Gets the category id. Tenant-local, and resolvable through `/v1/financials/item-categories`.

name.description:
Gets the category's name. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL`, and practice-renamable.
    Categories HAS NO DELETE FLAG, so deletion there is hard AND CASCADES:
FK_ItemCategories_Categories is ON DELETE CASCADE, so deleting a category silently
removes it from every item that carried it. See GET /v1/financials/items for what that means for a change
feed.

PublicCategoryReference.description:
A category, as it appears in an item's `categories[]`. Two fields only; `/v1/financials/item-categories`
    carries the full set.
    Categories are a MANY-TO-MANY through ItemCategories, so an item can have none, one or many, and
the array is empty rather than null when it has none.

creditNoteNumber.description:
Gets the practice-facing credit note number. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL` with a uniqueness
constraint, so it is `required` rather than nullable.

patientId.description:
Gets the patient this credit note belongs to, or NULL when it belongs to no patient.
    A credit note CAN EXIST WITHOUT A PATIENT: CreditNotes.PatientID is INT NULL, which
makes this aggregate unique among the three — Invoices.PatientID and
Estimates.PatientID are both NOT NULL. A null here is the practice's data, not a bug
and not a redaction. It also means the patientId filter can never return such a credit note.

invoiceId.description:
Gets the invoice this credit note was raised against, or null when it was raised standalone.
`INT NULL` with `FK_CreditNotes_Invoices`, so the reference resolves through
`GET /v1/financials/invoices/{id}`.

patientCreditId.description:
Gets the patient credit this note is settled through, or null.
    A REFERENCE ONLY. The patient-credit aggregate is not part of the public surface in v1, so this id is
not resolvable yet; it is published because it is the join key a consumer will eventually need, and
because it distinguishes a credit note backed by a live patient credit from one that is not — which
is exactly the distinction decimal? PublicCreditNote.AppliedAsPaymentAmount and decimal? PublicCreditNote.RefundedAmount
being null carries.

serviceLocationId.description:
Gets the location the service was delivered at, or NULL when the practice never set one.
`ServiceLocationID` is `INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` in the database and 0 is a "not set"
sentinel rather than a location id, so it is published as `null`: returning 0 would name a
location that does not exist.

billingLocationId.description:
Gets the location the credit note is billed from, or NULL when the practice never set one. Same
`NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` sentinel as int? PublicCreditNote.ServiceLocationId.

effectiveDate.description: Gets the effective date. A `DATE` column — a calendar date with no time part.

createdUtcDate.description:
Gets the creation timestamp, in UTC.
    MAY BE 1900-01-01T00:00:00Z. The column is DATETIME NOT NULL with a
DEFAULT '1900-01-01', so a credit note written before the platform started recording creation
timestamps carries that sentinel rather than a real date. Such a row is returned like any other; if
it has also never been edited, DateTimeOffset PublicCreditNote.ModifiedDateUtc equals the sentinel and the row sits
permanently at the front of the change feed.

status.description:
Gets the lifecycle state. `Void` and `Deleted` credit notes ARE part of the feed and are
returned with their status, so filter on `status` rather than assuming a live-only collection.

subTotalAmount.description:
Gets the sub-total amount. GROSS of discount: the platform computes it as the line sub-totals with
decimal PublicCreditNote.TotalDiscount added back, so `subTotalAmount - totalDiscount` is the net figure
and this one is not.

totalDiscount.description: Gets the total discount applied across the credit note's lines.

amount.description:
Gets the credited total — what the practice gave back. Computed by the platform as
`subTotalAmount - totalDiscount + the credit note's tax total`, and that last term is the sum of
the unpublished `CreditNoteTaxes` rows, so on a taxed credit note this figure does NOT reconcile
from the published fields alone. It is authoritative; do not recompute it.

appliedAsPaymentAmount.description:
Gets how much of the credit has been spent as payment, or NULL.
    NUMERIC(18,2) NULL and published as nullable deliberately. The write path sets it to null —
not zero — when the credit note has no live patient credit behind it, so "never applied" and
"applied zero" are genuinely different facts and coalescing would assert the second when the first is
true. A consumer that wants a number must choose its own default and know it is choosing.
    Together with decimal? PublicCreditNote.RefundedAmount and decimal PublicCreditNote.Balance it accounts for
decimal PublicCreditNote.Amount: appliedAsPaymentAmount + refundedAmount + balance == amount, treating
each null as zero. That is a REAL invariant here, not a tautology — all four values are stored
independently in their own columns, unlike the invoice surface's paidAmount, which is derived
from amount - balanceDue and therefore closes by construction.

refundedAmount.description:
Gets how much of the credit was refunded in cash, or NULL, on exactly the same terms as
decimal? PublicCreditNote.AppliedAsPaymentAmount — the two are set and cleared together.

balance.description:
Gets the unconsumed remainder of the credit, as the platform maintains it against the linked patient
credit's outstanding amount. `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, so unlike the two figures above this one is
always a number: a credit note with no live patient credit reads `0` here and `null` there.

currency.description:
Gets the currency. Fixed `"USD"`: the platform stores no currency per credit note, so this
states the assumption every amount above is denominated in rather than leaving a consumer to infer it.

modifiedDateUtc.description:
Gets the change-feed watermark: `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)`, in UTC.
    NON-NULLABLE by construction. The stored ModifiedUtcDate is nullable and is null for every
credit note nobody has edited; publishing that directly would make those rows invisible to a consumer
syncing on it, so this field carries the coalesced value and equals createdUtcDate until the
first edit. The query parameter that filters on it is updatedSince — the asymmetry between the
two names is deliberate and platform-wide.

lineItems.description:
Gets the lines, ordered by `orderIndex` then id. Fetched set-based for the whole page: one query
for the headers and one for every line on the page.

PublicCreditNote.description:
A credit note: the header plus its lines.
    Property order is the wire order. The header drops CreatedByUserID, ModifiedByUserID, the
legacy nullable LocationID superseded by the service/billing pair, SharedWithPatient,
Reference, and the operator free text Notes, Reason and Description.
    CreditNoteTaxes, CreditNoteMemberships, CareCreditRequests and the
PatientCredit aggregate are never joined. The patient credit in particular: the internal read
attaches it with its whole AppliedPatientCredits collection, each carrying a nested
Payment, so int? PublicCreditNote.PatientCreditId is a REFERENCE ONLY and the applied and refunded
figures below come from the credit note's own columns rather than from that graph.
    THERE IS NO TAX FIELD ON THIS PAYLOAD, and a consumer must not read the absence as an implicit zero.
CreditNotes carries no tax column whatsoever: no TaxTotal, no
TaxableSubTotalAmount, no NonTaxableSubTotalAmount, and — unlike both Invoices and
Estimates — not even CoveredTaxesAmount. There is no SurchargesTotal and no
TipsTotal here either. A taxed credit note's tax sits in the CreditNoteTaxes breakdown
rows, which v1 drops, so it is unavailable rather than zero.
    There are no responsibleParties: no such table exists for credit notes at all, which is a
stronger statement than the one the invoice and estimate surfaces make, where the table exists and the
slice cuts it.

parentCreditNoteItemId.description:
Gets the line this one hangs under, or null when it is a top-level line. Package and adjustment lines
form a hierarchy. `FK_CreditNoteItems_ParentCreditNoteItems` keeps the reference resolvable
within `CreditNoteItems`, but it does NOT constrain the parent to the same credit note — so
resolve a parent within the `lineItems` array you were given rather than assuming it is there.

itemId.description: Gets the catalog item id this line was created from. Resolves through `GET /v1/financials/items/{id}`.

overrideName.description:
Gets the display name the practice typed on this line, or null when they typed none.
    OPERATOR-AUTHORED FREE TEXT and it MAY CONTAIN PHI, because a practice can type anything into it — a
procedure, a body site, or a patient's own words. Treat it as protected health information:
do not log it, do not put it in a cache key, do not index it for search, and do not display it
outside an authorized clinical or billing context.
    NVARCHAR(100) NULL per the DACPAC — nullable HERE, unlike the invoice and estimate lines where
the same column is NOT NULL. So null and an empty string are both reachable, and they
mean the same thing.

orderIndex.description:
Gets the position of this line within its credit note, ascending. `INT NOT NULL`, so always
present.

rate.description:
Gets the rate. A UNIT PRICE unless bool PublicCreditNoteLineItem.IsCalculatedRate is `true`, in which case this
IS the line total and multiplying by decimal PublicCreditNoteLineItem.Quantity is wrong.

isCalculatedRate.description:
Gets a value indicating whether decimal PublicCreditNoteLineItem.Rate is the line total rather than a unit price — the
    case a price schedule produces.
    When false: subTotalAmount = rate × quantity − totalDiscount. When true:
subTotalAmount derives from rate alone and the multiplication does not reconcile.
subTotalAmount is authoritative either way; this flag says which arithmetic applies, so a
consumer does not read a price-schedule line as an arithmetic bug. The column carries the identical
